steps.content: The autumn wasteland night bites deep. Starlight is now a cold, punctured white, like countless tiny rents in the fabric of the dark, gazing down on the barren earth and the lost souls wandering beneath.
By the campfire, the fallen Campbell heiress huddles, hugging her knees. Even the flames cannot warm the grey pallor of her face. The food Rust prepared sits untouched and cold beside her.
She does not blink. Her eyes are fixed on the embers as they slowly die.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...I won't go.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I won't go anywhere except Furor.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Ms. Margaret entrusted me to reach the leaders of the farland settlements. She said Fraser is moving against everyone, that preserving peace means stopping their schemes... I must go.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: While bearing that torturous sorcery?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: You promised her you would help me!

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: What? You still want to save the person who betrayed us? Did the Tide of Ashes clog your brain with sand?

Her emotions clot in her throat before she can voice them. Rust's resolve is unyielding, and Hypatia, against her own will, trusts it. It's that very trust that now saturates her with a sorrow that feels ancient and absolute.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Do you judge me a burden? Because I can't withstand the Luminaris Society's sorcery? Because I...
...keep failing?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You know that isn't what I meant.
Rust's voice softens. He sets the still-warm cup of tea in her hands, taking her cold plate away. He then feeds more charcoal to the fire and watches, silent, as the embers fight to catch.
Only when the flames lift and steady does he seem to find his words.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I share Madam Margaret's high regard for you. The peace you have envisioned together is truly moving. I admire everything you've both done.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But she is, after all, <color=#fb9259>DisCity's</color> Peace Ambassador. However deep your friendship runs, Margaret holds an unshakable position. And trust me, that position does not align with yours.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You don't owe the Outland Affairs Officer your compliance. You've already gathered ample intelligence for her and scouted the dangers ahead. It's enough; she'll be satisfied.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Just look at how the Luminaris researchers have reacted. The Fraser authorities have already factored you into their schemes. The plots aimed at you are as thick as those targeting other leaders. If Margaret truly considered you a friend, she would agree to keep you off that field.
He says reassuringly, retrieving a thin blanket from the ship and draping it around her shoulders, but the gesture only deepens her shivering.

This ship goes no further. He will not take another step with her. Her journey ends here. Her breathing shallows; the spiritual brand flares, making her blood feel like fire in her veins. She forces herself still.

...Calm. She must stay calm. Any outburst now would only prove his point—that she's a child to be soothed with empty comforts. She refuses that. The road ahead is a war for adults, and if she wants to walk it, she must first earn her place.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...It isn't only for Ms. Margaret. This is my... own judgment. My choice.

Hypatia fights the tremor in her limbs as the sorcery twists through her nerves. Clutching the fraying ends of her control, she forms each word with painstaking care, willing her voice to sound steady and resolute.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I am an Aurum Secretum scholar and Fraser's frontline Mania specialist. All theoretical data from the Luminaris Society has passed through my hands. I know they lack DisCity's accumulated technological foundation.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Fraser cannot purge the remnants of BR-005. Even if a mine emerges from the ruins, it'll be nothing but a contaminated death trap, human bait laced with Hypercubes.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Countless refugees will be deceived into walking straight into it, their lives becoming consumables for Fraser to harvest "resources," just like Furor before. I know this pattern too well. The tasks they once assigned me followed the same design.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: My city-state incites despair and hatred to control refugees; the Society I served uses truth to deceive believers; my research has been complicit in these crimes. Every comfort of my life has been built upon the suffering of others. And then... my brother...
She fights to stay steady, but at the mention of him, a tremor escapes her control.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Yes. The one who brought the suspicious individuals into Furor was Adelaide Campbell. He delivered the seed they called "inheritance" to the refugees. I believe you understand what that means, so you must also know what he has done.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...He is my brother. He led me out of the Campbell household, introduced me to experimental research, and opened doors for me. He was... once so close to me.

The past surges: tenderness and cruelty, sincerity and hypocrisy, colliding into dissonant shards that form memories beyond reason. Both the beautiful and the monstrous feel equally unreal, like pieces of the same fever dream.
The hand that once guided hers so gently was also steeped in blood. They had walked so closely that she must have walked in it, too, staining what she'd once believed was a path of light.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...He was that close to me. All of it happened where I could see. I understand what was done. Some things... I must do them myself.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Ms. Margaret, Hella, Yokna, Rael, Jabara... and all the people of Furor. They're waiting. I have to go. This time, I must make it in time.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: This is my... inescapable responsibility.
She tries to speak, but her voice fails. A gust of wind tears her words away, burying them under the snap and rustle of the weathered tarpaulin along the hull.

Rust watches her closely. The young scholar's pupils tremble, her lips pale. It's hard to tell whether the sorcery is strangling her reason, or if her own obsessive fixation is feeding the torment planted inside her.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...Responsibility...
He turns his gaze to the fire flickering against the dark.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: The responsibility to prevent tragedy... Being accountable to others...
The flames gutter, but he doesn't feed them this time. He only watches, his expression cooling with the embers, until it matches the night's chill.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: How far does that responsibility extend?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Huh?
When his gaze finds her again, there is no trace of the earlier kindness left in it.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Will you challenge Fraser, toppling political alliances they've nurtured for decades? Or will you hunt the Undergrounders, rooting out sewer rats even the 9th Agency couldn't catch?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: How far are you willing to go, and what price are you prepared to pay?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Is it responsibility driving you to this, or guilt? Do you truly wish to stop a conspiracy, or are you trying to atone for the past?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Or perhaps all that matters is that you suffer, treating this as your personal penance?
The protest rises, but she swallows it. Hypatia turns her head aside.
When she finally speaks again, the ideals have bled out of her voice. What remains is hollow—a dry, resolute echo.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...That doesn't matter, sir.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: What I think is irrelevant. Whatever the farlands need, I will do. I will offer everything a scholar can provide.
Rust feels a sudden, ironic urge to laugh. The things she calls "irrelevant" are perfectly clear to him, and he knows exactly how much trouble it would be to move the immovable rock before him.
...It's all too familiar. He knows he should stop here, but the words slip out anyway.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Then start by reclaiming what makes you most valuable as a scholar.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Recover your composure and your wisdom. See yourself clearly. See the world clearly, then you will understand...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You truly did your best. That things did not turn out perfectly... is not your failing.
His tone holds no warmth, but neither is it harsh—only steady and inevitable, like ever-shifting quicksand.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You cannot fight the sins of an entire city‑state. Nor can you reclaim loved ones who have fallen to corruption or simply drifted away.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: All distortion and suffering in the lands of famine stems from scarcity. Calamities have compressed humanity's living space. You cannot achieve a reversal unless you make the Perishing Star change its course...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: But none of us can do that.
It's like a sigh that arrives too late, a eulogy echoing from a distance, spoken before an audience that isn't there.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: The Black Ring born from the collective will... It's the terminal illness of our age. A fate chosen by so many. You can't undo that with a hero or two.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: To carry the burden of others, you must first abandon the past and walk alone into the future. That is the true responsibility of a survivor, and it is no lighter than seeking death or atonement...

At first, Hypatia doesn't grasp his meaning. But she notices something else: Rust is looking at her, yet through her. His gaze is fixed on something she can't see. A jarring dissonance settles in her mind, and the contradictions begin to surface.

Why would a DisCity agent, who only came recently, know so much about the Luminaris Society? How can he, her supposed ally against the Black Ring, wield the Underground sorcery? Why, after just accepting Ms. Margaret's request, does he break protocol and urge her to leave? And why now? Who is he seeing when he looks at her?
The questions knot together, tightening, until instinct pulls one thread loose. She asks it softly.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Did something... happen to you in the past?
Her question draws him back. His gaze clears, returning from some distant place to rest on her, present and solid.
Then, at last, his familiar smile returns.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Hmm? Interested in my past? That'd take more than one night to tell, and fabricating stories is an agent's essential skill. Still care to hear it?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Actually, never mind. Time's precious, and we're nearly at the appointed hour.
He's said too much. Rust's eyes flick skyward, where a violet star drifts past the zenith—the signal from his contact.
That person will be here soon. Time to finish the preparations.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: My friend will be here shortly to take you somewhere safe. Once you're clear of the interference, that little dove of yours should regain its strength. You'll be able to reach Margaret again.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: You can report to her then. The Peace Ambassador will soon step onto her own battlefield. The intelligence you've gathered will be a considerable asset. This time, you will not disappoint her expectations.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Don't worry. My old colleague isn't as fragile as she might seem to you. With her methods, that gala in Fraser will certainly achieve "peace," regardless of what the organizers intended.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: As for the Luminaris Society, the Underground, or the Black Ring... leave them to me. They're already my prey. You just need to pick whichever show you prefer. Infiltration, espionage, assassination, or explosions... take your pick.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Soon, the Fraser news channels will broadcast a brand-new spy blockbuster. Tune in and enjoy the show; thank you for your patronage in advance.
He turns to Hypatia, his expression softening.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Now then, Agent Campbell. If that excessive sense of responsibility is weighing you down to the point of suffocation, perhaps you should consider my advice.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Your brilliance should be directed toward a greater future, not crushed under the weight of guilt until you fall into a manipulator's trap and your talent withers prematurely.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Perseverance is admirable. But when the path ahead seems pitch black, there's no harm in waiting, showing patience before charging blindly ahead. Seek knowledge. Forge friendships. You may yet borrow light from unexpected places, illuminating paths you never knew existed.

Light... that illuminates paths? The phrase reaches her with perfect clarity, yet she can't recall what such light looks like. She tries to reconstruct it in her mind, gathering fragments of memory and shaping them into something that might resemble illumination.

And as the image takes shape, a sudden, profound longing rises in her chest. It feels like a thirst she never named, like a traveler sighting a mirage of water after crossing a desert—a yearning she cannot contain.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Where would it be?

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: I don't know. But it will appear. Because you are kind, principled, and just stubborn enough. Many will want to help you, and many more will need your help in return.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Keep moving forward, but always toward the light. Someday, the clouds before your eyes will disperse, and all the questions that trouble you now will find their answers.
A tremor runs through her. Memories surge, a flicker passing behind her clouded eyes, something like tears, or longing. In that moment, Rust knows his words have struck true.
Finally, a crack appears in the armor of her composure. Hypatia's lips part, desperate for more.
...But the words never come. They die unspoken, dissolving into a whisper of defeat.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...Hah... There I go again... Always like this...

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...What is it?
When she lifts her head again, the stubborn rock is armored once more. Hypatia looks Rust squarely in the eye and delivers her answer, each word measured and precise.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I will take your advice and leave for safety with your friend. However, before that, I still wish to complete the one task that lies directly ahead of us.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...This isn't just about my personal obsession. It is also assistance you will greatly need for what comes next.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I suspect that after sending me away, you intend to go to the Furor ruins alone. Am I wrong? You called those people your prey; you won't stand idle while their conspiracy unfolds.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: But the Luminaris Society's intelligence network is exceptionally complex. No matter how capable you are, you cannot decipher their data alone. I was once one of them, so I understand their systems, and I have conducted extensive research on Furor. That is precisely what you need now, isn't it?
Rust says nothing, perhaps surprised by the girl's sudden poise, perhaps genuinely considering her words.
Hypatia uses the silence. She stands and offers a deep, formal bow.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I apologize. I know I have been stubborn. I've caused you trouble throughout this journey, and now I make such a request. But before I can move forward with resolve... I must fulfill this duty.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I give you my word: during the operation, I will follow every command and will not complicate matters. Once I have provided the necessary support and ensured the safety of the farland leaders, I will leave Fraser exactly as you arrange.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...You may say suffering is inevitable in this land, but my intuition as a scholar tells me the moment for change has finally come. BR‑005 was a devastating blow, yet it is also the hope they have waited for so long. This is the most critical juncture.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: I want to contribute, too. And there are things I can do now. If my skills are insufficient for field operations, then perhaps you could instruct me, Master? I should at least qualify as a somewhat talented student... shouldn't I? After all, I did manage to capture you three days ago.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: ...I'm not entirely without worth. Am I?

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Please. I am asking you.
Hypatia manages an uneven smile through swollen, red-rimmed eyes, and for a moment, a genuine brightness pierces the night.
How cruel that such light has fallen upon this dark, desolate wasteland.

Rust finally understands: he cannot move this stubborn rock alone. His gaze shifts toward the horizon. His contact hasn't arrived, but a different, fainter light glides in from the opposite direction, moving toward the plain.
It's someone else. He recognizes it instantly.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Hm... Not mine. Fraser pursuers, perhaps? Seems we were too engrossed in conversation and missed our window. We'll wait for the next one.
He rises, calmly smothers the campfire, and calculates the distance and timing. Enough time remains. Brushing his hands clean, he turns to Hypatia.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Well. Now we've got plenty of extra time. Anything else you wish to do? Tell me, I'll see it through with you to the end.

steps.speaker: Hypatia
steps.content: Thank you. I'm sorry to impose, but... thank you. I will give it everything I have!

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: Alright, alright. It's fine. I saw this coming.

steps.speaker: Rust
steps.content: ...I understand.
He covers their traces with sand, tosses the still-warm fire remnants onto the sand ship, then signals his contact and boards to reconfigure their route.
They'll take the long way, through high-risk territory to break any trail, before circling toward their true destination.
Sooner or later, she must return to the beginning: to see the ruins of Furor with her own eyes.
In Fraser City
The sky hangs low, a veil of gray gauze blurring Fraser's firmament. Yet the nobility's garden salon remains an island of fragrance and light, where laughter flows unchecked.
The hostess sits alone in a secluded corner, posture languid yet regal. With delicate fingers, she crumbles a honey cookie onto the table, smiling as small birds hop close to peck at the pieces.
A noble approaches quietly and takes the seat beside her.

steps.speaker: Fraser Noble A
steps.content: You seem somewhat preoccupied, Ms. Margaret. Not enjoying the salon?
Margaret's expression remains distant, still shadowed by unspoken worry.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Forgive me. My mind was elsewhere. A cherished canary of mine flew from my window some days ago. With the state of the world beyond our walls—the contamination, the sandstorms... I fear for the poor creature...

steps.speaker: Fraser Noble A
steps.content: A pity. If it ventured beyond the city... I fear the odds are grim. The wastes are fraught with more than calamities. But please, do not despair. I have several fine canaries at my estate. You would be most welcome to visit and select a new companion.
Margaret shows no offense. She only smiles and lets out a long, soft sigh.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You are too kind. But each creature has its own spirit, does it not? I was... particularly fond of that one...
After a long moment, Margaret rises to her feet.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: My apologies to everyone, but I must beg your indulgence and end this tea party early. A pressing matter requires my attention. Please, do continue to enjoy the afternoon.
With that, she gives a slight, graceful flourish of her fan and turns away, leaving the gathered Fraser nobles in speechless silence.
As she reaches the stairs, a figure steps smoothly into her path, blocking her descent.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Where are you heading to, ma'am?
Under Helga's icy gaze, Margaret's smile becomes a mask that gives nothing away.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Envoys from the Luminaris Society made an appearance at the farland meeting. Negotiations proceeded favorably. A joint expedition to the Furor ruins is now being discussed.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: We both know what Fraser truly seeks in those ruins.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: So... you can rush back home, or you can stay here and continue to watch me. The choice is yours.
Deep in WhiteSands

Starlight washes over the WhiteSands, glazing a landscape thick with the mingled reek of rot and stagnant mire. An Aurum Secretum Warrior moves forward, flanked by a sleek Alchemic Beast that treks through the desert in silence.
A sudden vibration cuts the silence. The warrior retrieves a communicator and sees a message from the Luminaris Society.
The rat has fled, Saina. Track it. Terminate it.

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: Mission received.
She bends down, gently stroking the Alchemic Beast's head.

steps.speaker: Saina
steps.content: DisCity spy... I will kill you. I will spill your blood as an offering to my brothers and sisters!
